Tuairisc Bhainistíochta Mhíosúil an Príomhfheidhmeannach – 31ú Mí na Nollag 2025 
Chief Executive’s Monthly Management Report – 31st December 2025 
 
 
A Chara, 
I enclose the above report for your statutory consideration, this report has also been prepared under Section 136 
& 138 of the Local Government Act, 2001. The attached report is the Chief Executive’s Monthly Management 
Report for December 2025, detailing activities, updates and progress across various departments of Louth 
County Council. Key achievements and actions under various directorates from the Chief Executive Report for 
December 2025 include: 
 
1. Finance and System Support Directorate 
- 
Financial Performance: By 22 December, 95% of the annual budget was spent. Income collection stood 
at 94% of budget, with strong performance in Housing and Rates. Debtor management continued, with 
a closing balance of €45.9m. 
- 
ICT & Security: 645 IT support calls were logged (93% resolved). 14% of inbound emails were flagged 
as potentially harmful and blocked. Cybersecurity training focused on seasonal scams was delivered to 
elected members. 
- 
Website & Digital Services: Over 10,500 unique page views were recorded, with online planning and 
services pages most visited. Thursday was the busiest day for website activity. 
 
2. Economic Delivery Directorate 
- 
Economic Development: The Rates Waiver Scheme 2026 launched on 5th January to incentivise new 
businesses to occupy vacant premises in town and village centres. 
- 
Tourism: Our Festival Grants Scheme 2026 opened for applications in December. 
- 
Night-Time Economy: Drogheda’s Night Curation Fund supported successful events, strengthening the 
town’s alternative cultural scene. 
- 
Enterprise & Innovation: The Drogheda Digital Hub was officially opened by Minister for Enterprise, 
Tourism & Employment, Peter Burke, TD., providing state-of-the-art facilities for start-ups and remote 
workers.  
- 
Heritage: Drogheda’s rich heritage assets were showcased to the Minister for Heritage, Christopher 
O’Sullivan, TD on his visit to the town.  
- 
Planning activity remained high, with 88 applications received and robust enforcement of unauthorised 
development with 248no. Warning letters issued for the year to November, and 48no. Section 3 (1)(a) 
Notices – Directing the owner to carry out works to dangerous structures for the year to December 
2025. 
 
3. Operations & Environment Delivery Directorate 
- 
Municipal Operations: Extensive litter picking, bin emptying, road sweeping, and repairs were carried 
out across Dundalk, Cooley, Blackrock-Faughart, Drogheda, Ardee, and rural areas. Storm Bram 
required significant clean-up and drainage works. 
- 
Waste & Environment: 10 waste complaints were investigated; 161 litter investigations led to 24 penalty 
notices and two prosecutions.  
- 
Climate Action & Biodiversity: The Community Climate Action Fund supported 22 local projects. The 
Hare’s Corner biodiversity initiative launched for landowners. Louth County Council was nominated for 
the Green Public Sector of the Year Award 2026. 
- 
Facilities & Energy: Energy efficiency at County Hall improved to 34%. Upgrades were completed at 
Ardee Castle and Dundalk Fire Station. Refurbishment of the Cornmarket Building in Drogheda was 
finalised. 
- 
Emergency Services: Firefighter training and equipment upgrades continued. Major Emergency 
Management progressed with generator procurement for Community Support Centres. Civil Defence 
provided medical cover and community support. 
 
4. HR, Corporate & Community Delivery Directorate 
- 
During the month of December 2025 Customer Services dealt with 13,781 queries inclusive of 6,912 
calls, 862 e-mails and 6,007 counter queries. 
- 
Community support initiatives held during December included Putting your House in Order, Age 
Friendly Christmas bags and Christmas Wreath Making Workshop for the travelling community.

- 
The Local Enhancement Programme (LEP) 2026 was announced. The Department will allocate 
€239,207.33 to Louth LCDC. The programme will be administered through the Louth Local Community 
Development Committee (LCDC). 
- 
The ‘Louth Youth Leadership and Mentoring Project’ and the ‘PEACEPLUS Young People’s Outdoor 
Pursuits and Sports Leadership Programme’ were launched in December. 
- 
Louth Local Sports Partnership celebrated International Day for Persons with Disabilities on December 
6th at Dundalk Sports Centre. 
 
5. Housing & Culture Delivery Directorate 
- 
In 2025, under the ‘Housing for All’ (2022 – 2026) government plan, Louth County Council delivered 
562 new social housing units with an overall delivery to date of 1,608 units. This was achieved by a 
combination of LCC direct build, acquisitions (turnkey and Part V), and partnerships with Approved 
Housing Bodies. Arising from this, Louth County Council has exceeded the 2026 target of 1,376 social 
housing units 12 months early. While the Housing Section continues to work on delivering the existing 
pipeline, the focus will now shift to planning for delivery under the new government plan i.e. ‘Delivery 
Homes, Building Communities’ (2025 – 2030). 
- 
Homelessness & Housing: 252 people presented as homeless; 46 were placed in emergency 
accommodation. 28 housing allocations and 4 transfers were completed. The housing list stood at 
4,773. Rent arrears were actively managed, and 69 properties were void at month-end. 
- 
Maintenance & Grants: Over 1,000 maintenance requests were completed. 
- 
Affordable & Social Housing: Affordable Purchase Schemes progressed in Drogheda and Ardee.  
- 
Culture: The Archives hosted the “Intervals of Peace” exhibition. Libraries delivered the Science 
Festival, Jane Austen celebrations, and outreach to schools and IPAS centres. The Arts Office 
launched new grants and exhibitions. The Museum ran festive activities and acquired new artefacts. 
 
6. Major Capital Projects & Infrastructure Delivery Directorate 
- 
Ardee 2040 – submission of planning pack in December to An Coimisiun Pleanala, representing a key 
milestone for the project 
- 
€500,000 allocation under ORIS for the Boyne Greenway – North Bank 
- 
Urban Regeneration: Substantial completion was reached on St. Nicholas Quarter Phase 1. The 
Longwalk Urban Framework Plan advanced, and engagement continued on URDF Call 3 properties. 
- 
Placemaking & Public Realm: Projects progressed in Carlingford, Ardee, and Drogheda, including plaza 
and play space developments. 
- 
Transport & Greenways: Construction continued on the Narrow Water Bridge  
- 
The Boyne Greenway received €500,000 for enhancements.  
- 
Flood Defence & Marine: Flood relief projects in Dundalk, Drogheda, Baltray, Carlingford, and Ardee 
moved forward, with ecological works underway.  
- 
Schools & Community: Works at Ardee Educate Together NS progressed. Nine projects in North Louth 
received CLÁR funding. 
 
This report highlights some of the Louth County Council's progress across the various directorates in December 
2025.  
 
I would like extend my heartfelt thanks to all Louth County Council staff for their dedication and hard work 
throughout 2025.   
 
May I wish all councillors, staff and the community a peaceful and rewarding 2026!

Drogheda Digital Innovation Hub – Official 
Opening – Wednesday 17th December 
On 17th December, Minister for Enterprise, Tourism 
and Employment Peter Burke TD officially launched 
the Drogheda Digital Hub on Narrow West Street, 
marking a major step in Drogheda’s future 
development.  Initiated and developed by the 
Council with support from Enterprise Ireland under 
the Border Enterprise Development Fund, the hub 
offers state-of-the-art co-working spaces, meeting 
rooms, and technology infrastructure to support 
start-ups, remote workers, and scaling tech firms.  
Minister Burke highlighted its role in driving 
digitalisation and business growth in the North-East, 
while the Director of Economic Delivery emphasised 
its importance to revitalise the town and attract 
investment while also discussing the many further 
developments planned for Drogheda and the North-
East region.  Through programmes like Boyne 
Innovate and tailored training, the hub aims to foster 
entrepreneurship, collaboration, and economic 
renewal in Drogheda.

Exhibition Open to Public 
The “Intervals of Peace: The Civil War Prison Art of 
Alfred McGloughlin” exhibition is currently open to 
the public at Louth County Archives. The exhibition, 
which was officially launched last month by Cllr 
Dolores Minogue, Cathaoirleach of Ardee Municipal 
District, is free to attend.  
 
Alfred McGloughlin, who was an artist and a nephew 
of the leader of the 1916 Rising, Patrick Pearse, was 
an anti-Treaty supporter during the Civil War. While 
he was imprisoned from 1922 to 1923, he kept up his 
artistic endeavours by drawing fellow prisoners. 
Alfred’s grandson, Professor Tim McGloughlin, 
rediscovered the drawings in the 1980s among family 
belongings. After years of careful preservation, they 
were exhibited at Kilmainham Gaol and the Pearse 
Museum at St Enda’s, Rathfarnham in 2022 and 
2023.  
 
The portraits include a number of veterans of the 
Easter Rising and War of Independence. While some 
of the portraits are unidentified, it would be wonderful 
if local people who may have had a family member in 
prison at that time, came to visit the exhibition and 
see if they are able to identify any local person. 
 
The exhibition, which is free to attend, will run until 
the 26th of February 2026 during office hours. 
Contact the Archives Service on 042-9324358.
